formulas.name: C basics
f: Types : char 1 byte, int 24, float 4, double 8
notes: Where: sizes in bytes (int is 2 or 4 by compiler)
Tip: Execution starts at main(); statements end with ';'. printf format: %d int, %f float, %c char, %s string.
Example: int a = 7, b = 2: a/b = 3, a % b = 1, (float)a/b = 3.5. x = 5; y = x++; → y = 5, x = 6.

f: 2-D array int b[3][4] stored row by row
notes: Tip: The array name is the address of the first element. C does no bound checking. A string is a char array ending with the null character.

notes: Tip: Recursion needs a base case: fact(n) = n × fact(n − 1), fact(0) = 1. Storage classes: auto, static, extern, register.

mcqs.q: Q1. In C, a[i] is equivalent to
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) *(a + i) Array name is the address of a[0].

mcqs.q: Q2. Which architecture uses separate program and data memories?
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) Harvard Used in DSPs and microcontrollers.

mcqs.q: Q3. The operator that gives the address of a variable is
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) & * gives the value at an address.

mcqs.q: Q4. int a[5]; — index of the last element
mcqs.ans: Ans: (a) 4 C arrays start at index 0, so a[0] … a[4].

mcqs.q: Q5. int x = 10, *p = &x; the value of *p is
mcqs.ans: Ans: (b) 10 * dereferences the pointer: the value stored at the address in p.
Ans: (a) 3 Integer division drops the fraction.

mcqs.q: Q7. Which is NOT a C storage class?
mcqs.ans: Ans: (d) dynamic The storage classes are auto, register, static and extern.

mcqs.q: Q9. Which memory loses its data when power is switched off?
mcqs.ans: Ans: (c) RAM RAM is volatile; ROM, flash and disks are non-volatile.
